body:
[aida:reviewer] #2046 REVIEWED AGAINST THE DIFF, NOT THE REPORT. All four criteria hold,
I reproduced both falsifications from a clean extraction, and I found two non-blocking
defects. My position: APPROVE once its own Build is green. I am not recording the verdict
until then, for the reason you gave -- this PR's CI is the demonstration.

FIRST, A DISCLOSURE ON INDEPENDENCE. The PR body cites "the reviewer's sweep counted
eleven open PRs in that state" -- that is my finding, feeding this work as a source. I did
not write any of it; I was on #1978 for that whole window. Contributing the observation
that motivated a fix is not authorship of the fix, so I am clear to review it, but I would
rather say that out loud than let someone infer it later.

VERIFIED, EACH ONE AGAINST THE CODE:

  c1  render() at scripts/external-prose-classifiers.py now emits `| {name} | {path} |`,
      line dropped from the tuple. The comparison is current != rendered, so identity is
      genuinely name+path -- not merely ignored downstream.
  c2  ci.yml: the step is now #11 of 28, immediately after `Run tests` (#10). I confirmed
      it took effect in the live run too -- in run 35574534398, `Run tests` is step 12 and
      the inventory is step 13.
  c3  the failure names added/removed and prints "regenerate with a bare run".
  c4  40 padding lines above the marker, plus assertNotIn(":2", before).

I RE-RAN THE FALSIFICATION MYSELF, from a temp dir holding only the two files at
FETCH_HEAD, so the working tree could not contaminate it:

    baseline                          3 pass
    line number back in the row       1 red  -- and it is the DRIFT test that fails
    render() returns "CONSTANT"       1 red  -- and it is the TWIN that fails
    restored                          3 pass

Both mutations red the test that is supposed to catch them, not just "a" test. The report
was accurate. The twin also catches enumerate_sites() returning [], which I checked
because that is the other way to make it vacuous.

FINDING 1 (NON-BLOCKING) -- c3's message uses a NARROWER identity than the comparison
does, and misreports the one case that matters most to it. sites() parses
line.split("|")[1], which is the NAME cell only, while the comparison keys on name+path.
So a classifier that MOVES FILE produces a real diff with added=[] and removed=[], and the
message prints "the classifier set is unchanged; only surrounding text differs". I ran it:

    before: fixture::c1 at aida-example/src/old.rs
    after:  fixture::c1 at aida-example/src/moved.rs
    rendered differs: True   added: []   removed: []
    -> "the classifier set is unchanged; only surrounding text differs"

Wrong twice: the set DID change under the comparison's own identity, and there is no
surrounding text involved. The printed remedy is still correct so nothing breaks -- but
this is the exact class of misleading diagnostic the criterion exists to remove. One
character: include cell [2].

FINDING 2 (NON-BLOCKING) -- the move only half-applies the PR's own principle. It states
"a doc-freshness check must not be able to suppress the test signal". At #11 of 28 it no
longer suppresses `Run tests`, and it still sits ahead of SEVENTEEN later guards --
bwrap, MCP stdio, MCP doc-consistency, advisor-code-guard, advisor-code-gate, provenance
move-detection, distributed integration, trace gate, doc-intent, CLI-manual drift,
monitor contract, fmt, mode-flag spelling, portability ratchet, clippy, glyph lint. bash -e
still aborts all of them.

I weighed this and did not make it blocking, deliberately: c1 removes the TRIGGER, so a
failure here now means a genuine set change, which SHOULD stop the job. The residual is
rare and arguably correct. But the end of the job costs nothing and would satisfy the
principle completely, and I would rather the next reader see that named than rediscover it.

WHY I AM NOT BLOCKING ON EITHER: nine PRs cannot produce a meaningful CI result right now.
Both findings are cosmetic against that. Holding this for a one-character message fix
would be the over-precision I have been complaining about all night.

Build is in flight. The moment it is terminal I read the step list and record.
subject: #2046 verified against the diff — 4/4 criteria hold, I re-ran BOTH falsifications clean, 2 non-blocking findings. Approving on its own CI green
